title: 我们如何利用威尔逊置信区间和贝叶斯推断构建虚假评价检测系统
author: gobuy.ai
content:
When we started building GoBuy, we had one question: can math tell you whether those 4.9-star reviews are real?

The answer is: not with certainty, but with confidence. And the difference between certainty and confidence is where the interesting engineering lives.

The Problem

Amazon has over 300 million products. Conservative estimates suggest 30-40% of reviews are fake, AI-generated, or incentivized. The problem is getting worse, not better — LLMs can generate thousands of convincing reviews in minutes.

Existing tools (Fakespot, ReviewMeta) use proprietary black-box methods. We wanted something transparent: a scoring system where every number is derivable from first principles.

The Stack: Three Mathematical Layers

Layer 1: Wilson Score Lower Bound

The foundation of every GoBuy Smart Score is the Wilson Score Interval — specifically, the lower bound of a binomial proportion confidence interval.

If a product has 500 reviews and 480 are positive (96%), the naive average is 0.96. But how confident are we that the true positive rate is 0.96? The Wilson interval answers this: 

Lower bound = (p + z²/(2n) - z·√(p(1-p)/n + z²/(4n²))) / (1 + z²/n)

Where:

  • p = observed positive proportion (0.96)
  • n = sample size (500)
  • z = z-score for confidence level (1.96 for 95% confidence)

For our example: the Wilson lower bound is 0.938, not 0.96. That's a meaningful difference when comparing products.

Why this matters: A product with 10 reviews at 100% positive has a Wilson lower bound of 0.69 — barely better than a coin flip. A product with 1,000 reviews at 95% positive has a Wilson lower bound of 0.935. The math naturally penalizes small samples.

Layer 2: Bayesian Beta Posterior

Wilson gives us a snapshot. But reviews accumulate over time, and we want to update our beliefs incrementally. Enter the Beta-Binomial model.

We model each product's true quality as a draw from a Beta distribution: 

Quality ~ Beta(α, β)

Where α = positive reviews + 1 (prior pseudo-count) and β = negative reviews + 1.

The Beta posterior is conjugate to the Binomial likelihood, which means we can update it in closed form as new reviews arrive — no MCMC, no approximations, just arithmetic.

The posterior mean is α / (α + β) — which naturally shrinks toward 0.5 (uncertainty) when review counts are low, and converges to the true positive rate as data accumulates.

We use the 5th percentile of the posterior (the lower credible bound) as our quality estimate. This is more conservative than the posterior mean and provides the same "benefit of the doubt goes to skepticism" principle as the Wilson bound.

Layer 3: Temporal Anomaly Detection

A product with 2,000 genuine reviews and 500 fake reviews added in a 48-hour window should raise red flags — even if the overall positive rate looks fine.

We compute a review velocity signature: the rolling rate of review arrival over time, segmented by verified/unverified status and rating value. Sustained spikes in 5-star reviews from unverified purchasers are the strongest signal of coordinated manipulation.

We use a simple exponential weighted moving average (EWMA) of review sentiment over time. Products whose recent reviews are systematically more positive than their historical baseline receive a temporal penalty.

Putting It Together: The Smart Score

The final GoBuy Smart Score (0-100) is a weighted combination:

Component Weight Source
Wilson lower bound 35% Review volume + sentiment
Bayesian posterior (5th pct) 30% Updated quality estimate
Temporal consistency 20% Velocity + trend analysis
Verification rate 10% Verified purchase ratio
Text authenticity 5% Heuristic AI-generated review detection

Every component is auditable. Every score is reproducible. No black boxes.

The MCP Layer for AI Agents

Here's where it gets interesting for developers. GoBuy exposes an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets AI agents query trust scores in real-time: 

result = await mcp_client.call_tool("gobuy_check_trust", {
    "product_url": "https://amazon.com/dp/B08X4ABCD"
})

This means any AI shopping agent can make trust-aware decisions — filtering out suspicious products before recommending them to users.

What We Learned

  1. Transparency beats complexity. Our scoring is simpler than Fakespot's, and that's a feature. Users and developers can understand exactly why a product scores 34/100.

  2. Small samples are the enemy. The biggest mistake in review analysis is trusting products with few reviews. Wilson and Beta both handle this naturally — you don't need a complex model to know that 10 reviews aren't enough.

  3. Temporal signals are critical. The pattern of when reviews arrive matters as much as what they say. A 48-hour 5-star burst is never organic.

  4. AI agents need trust scores more than humans do. A human can read reviews critically. An AI agent consuming a product database cannot — it needs a pre-computed trust signal.

GoBuy is live at gobuy.ai. Check any Amazon product's trust score, or integrate our MCP server into your AI agent. API docs here.
aiSummary: GoBuy 结合威尔逊置信区间、贝叶斯 Beta-二项分布更新以及时间异常检测，构建了一套透明、可审计的虚假评价检测系统，并通过 MCP 服务器供 AI 智能体调用。
oneSentenceSummary: GoBuy 结合威尔逊置信区间、贝叶斯 Beta-二项分布更新以及时间异常检测，构建了一套透明、可审计的虚假评价检测系统，并通过 MCP 服务器供 AI 智能体调用。
summary: 为了在不依赖不透明黑盒模型的情况下解决电商中虚假及 AI 生成评价泛滥的问题，GoBuy 设计了一套透明的评价信任评分系统。该框架采用三层数学架构：利用威尔逊得分下限自然惩罚小样本量；使用共轭贝叶斯 Beta-二项后验分布，通过闭式算术进行增量质量估算更新；借助指数加权移动平均（EWMA）检测时间流速异常，如协同刷好评的爆发期。最终生成的 0–100 分 Smart Score 将这些统计指标与购买验证、文本真实性启发式规则相结合，并通过 MCP 工具向 AI 导购智能体开放，以实现具备信任感知的智能推荐。

mainPoints.point: 威尔逊得分下限自然惩罚小样本量
mainPoints.explanation: 系统没有依赖简单的平均评分，而是计算威尔逊区间下限，确保只有少量满分评价的商品相比拥有庞大、稳定评价基数的商品获得更为保守的得分。

mainPoints.point: 共轭 Beta-二项先验实现高效增量质量更新
mainPoints.explanation: 将评价情感建模为 Beta 分布，无需 MCMC 或近似算法即可实现闭式后验更新，并使用第 5 百分位数作为保守的置信下限。

mainPoints.point: 时间流速特征揭示协同操纵行为
mainPoints.explanation: 系统利用 EWMA 趋势分析标记在极短时间窗口内未经验证的 5 星好评集中爆发，当近期评分明显偏离历史基准时施加惩罚。

mainPoints.point: 通过 MCP 开放信任评分赋能自主 AI 智能体
mainPoints.explanation: 由于 AI 导购智能体在处理商品数据流时缺乏人类的鉴别力，通过模型上下文协议（MCP）工具提供可审计的信任评分，能够实现可靠的自动化推荐过滤。

keyQuotes: 现有工具（如 Fakespot、ReviewMeta）采用专有的黑盒方法。我们希望构建一套透明的评分系统：其中的每个数字都可以从第一性原理推导得出。
一个拥有 10 条 100% 好评的商品，其威尔逊下限仅为 0.69——几乎只比抛硬币好一点点。
数学机制会自然惩罚小样本。
48 小时内的 5 星好评集中爆发绝不可能是自然产生的。
AI 智能体比人类更需要信任评分。人类可以带着批判性眼光阅读评价，而摄入商品数据库的 AI 智能体却做不到——它需要一个预先计算好的信任信号。
